review.dimension: ADVERSARIAL TEST OF THE CHANGED LOGIC (engine_noshow.py F-GPS-LOGIC, DT-CW-NOSHOW R8/R11, AUTH-02 trigger 12, CW-F04/CW-F04B text as an LLM would apply it)
checked_ok: The engine's F-GPS-LOGIC covers every outside ping in the window. A ping in [start, wend] that is set aside lands in set_aside, because start >= t_arr >= lo_t whenever arrival is TRUE. A kept outside ping lands in edge_out whenever presence is CONSISTENT or SPARSE. So an automatic uphold needs every window ping inside the area, and the tests below agree.

Targeted cases: 47 in /tmp/a3check1/cases.py plus 10 more, each run through the full E.run on the new engine and on a pre-A3 snapshot (git archive de53c7c). They cover outliers at the arrival, at wend, 1 to 5 s after wend and between lo_t and the arrival; data errors; duplicate timestamps; approach pings inside the window; pings 2 to 20 s either side of the arrival; a 250 s look-back; ARRIVAL_UNCONFIRMED; 60, 61 and 120 s gaps; jitter; Ryde on-demand and advance bookings; an organizer late driver_wait_start; with and without the platform check; a missing, duplicated or earlier driver_arrived event; reversed file order; fractional-second timestamps; an 80 m platform check. None upheld a fee at AUTO while FairRyde's logic decided. A07 (advance booking, arrival confirmed only later, window anchored at the scheduled time) was R8 AUTO before A3 and is R11 APPROVE now.

Independent random search (/tmp/a3check1/fuzz2.py): 7,500 cases over seeds 7, 8 and 9, with edge pings at +-1 to 65 s around the arrival, the window start, the window end and t_arr-300, and shuffled file order. The oracle uses raw pings only: an outside ping in the window, a non-approach outside ping in [t_arr-300, wend], an unconfirmed arrival, a gap over 300 s, or a moved start. Result: 0 AUTO upholds that violate it. The same oracle finds many violations on the pre-A3 engine (for example an AUTO R8 with an outside ping at 08:43:35), so it has teeth. The builder's fuzz_presence.py with a new seed (1500 cases, seed 99) gives 0 findings.

Builder's claim that R1 and R4 never rest on the logic holds. The aside set holds only outside pings (runs plus first_in-1), so setting aside can only turn non-confirmation into confirmation and can only remove a LEFT. LEFT needs an outside ping inside the window: a run spanning the window with no ping in it leaves win empty, which gives UNKNOWN. R1 always carries FRD-01 (early_press) and so is never AUTO. /tmp/a3check1/fuzz3b.py ran 2,500 cases with real excursions: all 287 R4 waivers have a raw outside ping in the window, and there are 0 counterexamples. The 'except a data error' caveat is not even needed.

findings.claim: This bug predates A3 and A3 did not change it. Pings are sorted by their timestamp string, not by time. When GPS timestamps in one case mix UTC offsets, a real two-minute departure is sorted out of place and set aside as an outlier, so the fee is upheld where the rules waive it. A3's trigger now holds the case at APPROVE, but the trace tells the reviewer the pings were outliers.
findings.evidence: Line 325: 'gps = sorted(gps_raw, key=lambda g: g["timestamp"])'. Line 518 then inserts the platform observation at the first obs with t >= t_arr in that string order. Control case (five pings 150 m out from 08:46:00 to 08:48:00, written +08:00): 'WAIVE_FEE R4 AUTO ... pres=LEFT'. The same instants written as +00:00 ('2026-09-13T00:46:00+00:00'): 'UPHOLD R11 APPROVE GL=True why=['set_aside'] ... pres=CONSISTENT', with step 9 reporting '5 outlier ping(s) set aside'. The pre-A3 engine gives 'UPHOLD R8 APPROVE'.
findings.failure_scenario: A feed writes some GPS timestamps in UTC and others in +08:00. The driver leaves for 120 s mid-wait, so the rules give R4 WAIVE. The engine upholds the fee (R11, APPROVE) and tells the reviewer the absence was a GPS outlier. The data pattern is rare, but the outcome is wrong and the explanation misleads the reviewer.
findings.suggested_fix: Sort by parsed time: sorted(gps_raw, key=lambda g: T(g['timestamp'])). Optionally flag mixed UTC offsets under DQ-04.

findings.claim: F-GPS-LOGIC, and the sensitivity row move through it, fires on pings that cannot affect the arrival or the presence. Examples are pings set aside between the arrival and a later window start (advance bookings, organizer late driver_wait_start), or before an arrival the platform check already confirms. This sends routine cases to approval (safe direction). CW-F04's text says 'none was set aside' without saying over which range.
findings.evidence: Line 725: 'lo_t = (t_arr - timedelta(seconds=maxgap)) if t_arr is not None else start'. Line 726: 'aside_ids = [... lo_t <= obs[k]["t"] <= wend]'. A02 (Ryde advance booking, at the pin from 08:38, one 150 m outlier at 08:40:10, window 08:45:00 to 08:48:00): 'UPHOLD R11 APPROVE | old UPHOLD R8 AUTO | GL=True ['set_aside']'. G01 (organizer wait start 08:44, outlier 08:43:30): 'R11 APPROVE | old R8 AUTO'. O05 (platform check at 08:43, outlier at 08:42:00): 'R11 APPROVE | old R8 AUTO'. A03 (90 s pre-wait excursion, not set aside): 'R8 APPROVE ... LEFT_MIN_OUTSIDE_S'. O06b (outlier 6 min before the arrival): 'R8 APPROVE ... PING_MAX_GAP_S', because the high end (420) moves lo_t.
findings.failure_scenario: An advance-booking driver arrives 7 minutes early and has one GPS bounce while parked. The window from the scheduled time is clean and the platform check confirmed the arrival. The case still goes to APPROVE, and before A3 it was AUTO. Advance bookings with early arrivals are a plausible, recurring pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Count a set-aside ping only if it lies in [start, wend], or, without a platform check, in the moment-ping range [t_arr - PING_MAX_GAP_S, t_arr + TS_TOLERANCE_S] and before the confirmation. Alternatively, state the wider range in CW-F04 and CW-F04B and accept the cost in open_items.

findings.claim: CW-F04B words the later-confirmation item as conditional on the start moving ('so the wait start moved'), but the engine sets F-GPS-LOGIC on ARRIVAL_UNCONFIRMED whether or not the start moved. A literal LLM applier would rate an advance booking whose start stays at the scheduled time as F-GPS-LOGIC false, R8 and AUTO. In that case CW-F03B's start test is also skipped.
findings.evidence: rules.yaml line 598: 'the arrival was confirmed only by a later ping, so the wait start moved (ARRIVAL_UNCONFIRMED, CW-F03B)'. findings.suggested_fix: Reword the item as: 'the arrival was not confirmed at the indication and only a later ping confirmed it (ARRIVAL_UNCONFIRMED, CW-F03B), whether or not the wait start moved'.

An organizer twin with pings 90 s apart gives the same result. (b) Waiting fee, from the rule text: in E07 the free wait runs 10:14:30 to 10:17:30, with inside pings at 10:14:30 and 10:16:00 (0 m) and a platform check 'within 7m'. At the base values F-GPS-LOGIC is false, so AUTH-02 trigger 12 (rules.yaml 1759-1762) does not fire. At PING_MAX_GAP_S=60 presence is SPARSE (largest gap 90 s). CW-R05 has no presence condition, and CW-R12 escalates only WEAK+SPARSE, so the outcome stays UPHOLD. decisive_definition clause 2 (rules.yaml 53-55) counts only an outcome change or a row move, and a waiting fee has no rows. grep finds no text that extends the sensitivity test to F-GPS-LOGIC for waiting fees. The KB does extend the CW-F06 reading test to waiting fees explicitly (rules.yaml 658), but not the parameter test. So E07 stays AUTO while its no-show twin is APPROVE. Jasper's D29 lists 'the ping-gap and radius parameters'. D31 requires that waiting fees upheld on this logic also be APPROVE. The builder's D29 note relies on 'the sensitivity test ... as before', and for waiting fees that test has nothing to move. The A1b appliers already flagged the missing row-move test for waiting fees in kb_silent. This is not a regression: E07 was AUTO before A3 and the twin was APPROVE before A3. But A3 was the step meant to bring D29 to waiting fees, and the pattern is common: organizer gaps of 90 to 240 s exceed the 60 s low end. It is a tier difference in an in-scope type (CW-WAITING is adjudicated), so CRITICAL. Closing it needs either the trigger-12 extension or Jasper's recorded exemption.

The facts are reproduced. J02 (pings 3 m out, one at 15 m) and J03 (one ping at 45 m) give 'UPHOLD R8 AUTO' on the A2 engine and 'UPHOLD R8 APPROVE ... decisive: CW-F04B (... ARRIVAL_GEOFENCE_M moves within [10, 100])' on the A3 engine. The organizer profile with the platform 10 m check behaves the same. My own simulation (/tmp/a3check1/sk/sim_sk.py: 80 clean upholds, parked 0 to 20 m from the pin, jitter 3 to 5 m, both profiles) gives 45 AUTO before A3 and 8 after. The 37 that moved are all GPS-logic false with a window ping beyond 10 m, and the radius is the only trigger. The 8 that stay AUTO all have every ping within 10 m. fuzz_presence.py OFFS has 'in': 0.0, and selftest's _every puts inside pings exactly on VENUE, so neither covers jitter. The tier report says the clean variants 'still uphold automatically on R8'. The builder's D29 note says the parameters are handled 'as before', but the new R11 creates a row move at a radius of 10 m that did not exist before. So the effect is real, frequent and undisclosed. Whether it is wrong is Jasper's call: D29 names the radius parameters, and with R11 clause 2 now does exactly what D29 says. The sub-claim that an LLM applier will rule AUTO where the engine rules APPROVE is not shown: an applier that runs clause 2 at 10 m reaches R11 and APPROVE just like the engine. MAJOR applies if Jasper finds the radius effect unintended (a frequent tier shift, safe direction). If he accepts it, what remains is MINOR: tier report, the D29 'as before' wording, and tests without jitter.

Reproduced in /tmp/a3check1/sk/cases3.py. In the organizer clean case, pings 150 m out from 08:46:00 to 08:48:00 written with +08:00 give 'WAIVE_FEE R4 AUTO pres=LEFT'. Reproduced in /tmp/a3check1/sk/cases4.py. A02 is a Ryde advance booking: arrival with a platform check at 08:38, pings at the pin, one ping 150 m out at 08:40:10, window 08:45 to 08:48.
